sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of vitamins as tiny helper tools your body needs to get its jobs done. You only need a little bit of each, but you have to get them from food because your body can't make enough on its own. They are 'organic,' meaning they come from living things like plants and animals, unlike minerals, which come from rocks and soil.

### Question 2

Vitamins get sorted into two clubs based on what they can dissolve in, like sugar dissolving in water but oil not mixing with it. Some vitamins dissolve in fat and some dissolve in water. This matters a lot because it changes how your body stores them and how easily you can get too much or too little.

### Question 3

An easy way to remember the fat-soluble vitamins is the word ADEK, like a name. Those four ride around your body in fat. Vitamin C and all the B vitamins are the water-loving ones, so if you see a C or a B in the list, it does not belong in the fat club.

### Question 4

Water-soluble vitamins are like water in a cup with a hole in the bottom, extra just drains out in your pee. Fat-soluble vitamins are more like putting stuff in a closet, they get stored away and pile up. If you keep stuffing the closet, it can overflow and cause problems, which is why too much vitamin A or vitamin D, usually from supplement pills, can actually make you sick.

### Question 5

B vitamins are like the little keys that turn on the machines in your body that unlock energy from food. The food is the fuel, but without the keys the machines can't run. That is why B vitamins are called coenzymes, they team up with your body's workers (enzymes) to get energy out of what you eat.

### Question 6

Most vitamins are like groceries, you have to go get them from food. But vitamin D is special because your skin can actually build it when sunlight hits you, kind of like a tiny solar panel. That is why people call it the sunshine vitamin, and why you can run low on it in dark winter months.

### Question 7

Vitamin C is like the glue that holds your body's building materials together, especially the stuff called collagen in your skin and gums. Without enough glue, things start falling apart, gums bleed, cuts don't heal, and you bruise easily. That old sailor's disease called scurvy happened because they had no fresh fruit and ran out of vitamin C. The other choices are what happens when a different vitamin runs out: vitamin A keeps your night vision and eyes moist, vitamin K helps blood form scabs, and vitamin D helps you absorb calcium so bones stay hard.

### Question 8

That bright orange color in carrots and sweet potatoes comes from beta-carotene, which your body turns into vitamin A. So if you want more vitamin A from plants, reach for the orange veggies. Oranges give you vitamin C instead, and nuts give you vitamin E, so color and food type are good clues.

### Question 9

Vitamin C is a fragile, water-loving vitamin, so when you boil veggies for a long time it escapes into the water and gets wrecked by the heat. It is like washing colored chalk in a bucket, the color runs out into the water. Quick steaming or eating them raw keeps more of the vitamin inside the food.

### Question 10

When a baby is growing, its cells are dividing super fast, and folate is the vitamin that helps build brand-new cells and DNA correctly. Early on, the baby's brain and spine (the neural tube) form, and enough folate helps that happen without mistakes. That is why doctors want moms to get plenty of folate before and during early pregnancy.

### Question 11

Most vitamins hide in plenty of plant foods, but vitamin B12 is the tricky one, it comes almost entirely from animal foods like meat, eggs, and milk. So someone eating only plants can slowly run out unless they take a supplement or eat foods with B12 added. Without it, your blood and nerves start having trouble.

### Question 12

Vitamin K is the vitamin your body uses to make blood clot and stop bleeding, like the tools that seal a leak. You get it from leafy greens and also from helpful bacteria living in your gut. If antibiotics wipe out those bacteria and you don't eat greens, you run short, and cuts bleed longer and bruises appear easily.
